summary: Solomon Islands issues a free visitor's permit on arrival to citizens of some 70 countries — 90 days within 180 for EU, EEA and Swiss passports, 30 days (up to 90 in any 12 months) for the US, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and most Commonwealth and Pacific nationalities — while everyone else must obtain a visitor visa from the Immigration Division before traveling.

source.name: Solomon Islands Immigration Division — visitor's permit

fee.notes: Plus a USD 50 online lodgement fee. The page states both are levied in US dollars and converted to Solomon Islands dollars when the application is registered, and that they are usually non-refundable if the visa is refused.

source.name: Solomon Islands Immigration Division — Tourist Visa

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date you arrive in Solomon Islands.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 year and over arriving from, or having transited more than 12 hours through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

vaccinations.name: Malaria prevention
vaccinations.text: Malaria is present throughout Solomon Islands, including Honiara. There is no vaccine — discuss antimalarial tablets with a travel clinic before departure and use repellent and nets on the ground.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but medical facilities are very limited outside Honiara and serious cases are evacuated to Australia — cover including medical evacuation is strongly advised, especially for divers.

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed return or onward ticket is a condition of the visitor's permit and airlines routinely check it before boarding.

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must satisfy the officer that they can support themselves for the stay. No fixed figure is published. Carry evidence of accommodation and funds, such as a booking confirmation and a recent bank statement.

declarations.name: Arrival and customs declaration card
declarations.text: A combined immigration arrival and customs declaration card is handed out on the aircraft or at Honiara airport and must be completed before the immigration counter — pens are not always available, so carry one.

currencyLimits.text: Solomon Islands operates exchange controls: large amounts of cash must be declared on arrival and departure, and the amount of Solomon Islands dollars you may take out is restricted. Confirm the current threshold with Customs or the Central Bank before traveling with significant sums.

notes: Biosecurity is strict — fresh food, seeds, plants, timber, and unwashed dive or hiking gear must be declared and may be treated or seized.
Firearms, ammunition and offensive weapons are prohibited without a permit issued in advance by the Royal Solomon Islands Police Force.
Removing artefacts, war relics from the Guadalcanal campaign, coral, turtle shell or other protected wildlife products without a permit is an offense.

payments.text: Cards work at a handful of Honiara hotels, dive shops and supermarkets, and ATMs are essentially confined to Honiara, Gizo and Auki. Everywhere else is cash only — draw Solomon Islands dollars in the capital before flying to the provinces.

safety.text: Violent crime against visitors is uncommon and villages are welcoming, but petty theft occurs in Honiara and the capital has seen political unrest and rioting in the past. Avoid demonstrations, take care after dark, and monitor local news.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Solomon Islands travel information

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the drier, cooler season with the calmest seas and the best underwater visibility for diving the wrecks and reefs. November to April is hotter, wetter and inside the cyclone season.

tips.text: Malaria is present year-round across the whole country, Honiara included. See a travel clinic about antimalarials before you go, and sleep under a net and cover up at dusk once you arrive.

Outside Honiara there are almost no ATMs and cards are rarely accepted. Carry enough Solomon Islands dollars in small notes for your whole time in the provinces, including boat fares and village fees.

Almost all land, beaches and reefs are under customary ownership. Ask the local chief or landowner (and expect a modest fee) before walking, camping, surfing or diving — resorts and guides will arrange this for you.
Domestic flights and inter-island ships are frequently delayed or canceled by weather. Leave at least one buffer day before your international departure from Honiara.

The visitor's permit is capped at 90 days in total within any 12-month period, however many times you enter. Plan longer research, volunteering or dive seasons around that limit and apply to Immigration in advance if you need more.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Solomon Islands?
faq.answer: Probably not, if you hold a Western or Commonwealth passport. Citizens of EU, EEA and Swiss states enter without a visa for up to 90 days in 180, and citizens of the US, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and most Commonwealth and Pacific countries are given a free visitor's permit on arrival for 30 days. Everyone else must apply to the Immigration Division before traveling.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Solomon Islands as a tourist?
faq.answer: The visitor's permit issued at Honiara is normally 30 days and can be extended by the Immigration Division, but your total stay may not exceed 90 days within any 12-month period. EU, EEA and Swiss passport holders are admitted for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.

faq.question: What do I need to show at the border?
faq.answer: A passport valid at least 6 months, a confirmed onward or return ticket, proof of where you are staying and enough money for your visit, plus a completed arrival and customs card. Officers may also ask about your itinerary if you are traveling to the provinces.

faq.question: Can I extend my visitor's permit?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply at the Immigration Division in Honiara before your current permit expires, with your passport, ticket and proof of funds. Extensions are granted within the overall 90-days-in-12-months cap.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate?
faq.answer: Only if you are arriving from, or have spent more than 12 hours in transit in, a country with a risk of yellow fever transmission. Travelers coming directly from Australia, New Zealand, Europe, North America or Asia do not need one, but malaria prevention matters far more here.
